overview.headline: Secret Philadelphia convention that drafted new frame of government

keyPoints.point: The signed document established the government of the United States on September 17, 1787
keyPoints.quote: signed on September 17, 1787, established the government of the United States.

keyPoints.point: The Federal Convention convened in Philadelphia on May 14, 1787 to revise the Articles of Confederation
keyPoints.quote: The Federal Convention convened in the State House (Independence Hall) in Philadelphia on May 14, 1787, to revise the Articles of Confederation.

keyPoints.point: Members adjourned from day to day until a quorum of seven states was obtained
keyPoints.quote: the members adjourned from day to day until a quorum of seven states was obtained on May 25.

keyPoints.point: Delegates chose to draft an entirely new frame of government rather than amend existing Articles
keyPoints.quote: rather than amend the existing Articles, the Convention would draft an entirely new frame of government.

keyPoints.point: Chief points at issue included power of central government and representation in Congress
keyPoints.quote: Among the chief points at issue were how much power to allow the central government, how many representatives in Congress to allow each state

keyTerms.gloss: secret gathering of delegates who drafted the Constitution during summer
keyTerms.quote: Drafted in secret by delegates to the Constitutional Convention during the summer of 1787

keyTerms.gloss: earlier framework that the Convention met to revise in Philadelphia
keyTerms.quote: The Federal Convention convened in the State House (Independence Hall) in Philadelphia on May 14, 1787, to revise the Articles of Confederation.

keyTerms.gloss: minimum number of states required for members to conduct business
keyTerms.quote: the members adjourned from day to day until a quorum of seven states was obtained on May 25.

keyTerms.gloss: national authority whose power was debated among chief points at issue
keyTerms.quote: Among the chief points at issue were how much power to allow the central government, how many representatives in Congress to allow each state

keyTerms.gloss: individuals elected to serve voters or chosen by state legislators
keyTerms.quote: how these representatives should be elected—directly by the people or by the state legislators.
